explanations.answer: Where His wisdom and powers came from
explanations.explanation: That's the question, baker. They ask, "Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?" (Matthew 13:54). The text says they were astonished. I think they were saying it the way you'd say, "Hold on, who gave HIM the recipe?"

explanations.answer: When He will heal the sick in town
explanations.explanation: Nobody asks about healing here, friend. The people in the synagogue are astonished, and what they ask is, "Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?" (Matthew 13:54). It's a question about where it all came from. Nobody puts in an order for anything.

explanations.answer: How long He plans to stay in town
explanations.explanation: Nobody pulls out a calendar, baker. The text has Jesus teaching in the synagogue and the people astonished, and then they ask, "Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?" (Matthew 13:54). Their question is about where His wisdom and powers came from. The length of His visit never comes up.

Carpenter, baker. They ask, "Isn’t this the carpenter’s son?" (Matthew 13:55). To them, He's the one from the family they know. They name His mother, Mary, and four brothers, so they've clearly got the whole guest list memorized.
Not the fisherman, friend. The crowd asks, "Isn’t this the carpenter’s son?" (Matthew 13:55). Fisherman isn't in their question. I'd pack that answer away for another day.
Not the shepherd, baker. The hometown crowd asks, "Isn’t this the carpenter’s son?" (Matthew 13:55). They're pointing at what they know about His family. The word they use is carpenter.

Not this time, friend. The text says the opposite: "…they took offense at Him." (Matthew 13:57). They ask all those questions and end up offended, not honoring Him. Honor never shows up in the story, and Jesus says so Himself in the very next line.

False is right, baker. After the questions, the text says, "And they took offense at Him." (Matthew 13:57). So they're offended, not honoring Him. Jesus then says, "Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor."

explanations.answer: Only in his hometown and his own household
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. Jesus says, "Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor." (Matthew 13:57). He says it right after they take offense at Him. The word "only" is doing a lot of work in that line.

explanations.answer: Only in big cities and royal courts
explanations.explanation: Nice try, baker, but the grand places aren't mentioned. Jesus says, "Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor." (Matthew 13:57). He points to the places closest to home. No palace or city gets named.

It's the other way around, friend. Jesus says, "Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor." (Matthew 13:57). He names home, not strangers. Strangers and foreigners never come up in His line.

Right, baker. The text says, "And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief." (Matthew 13:58). Unbelief is the reason, and the verse says so plainly. I think that's a sad line, and I'd rather leave it just as the verse has it.

Noise isn't the reason, friend. The text says, "And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief." (Matthew 13:58). The verse gives unbelief as the reason. A noisy crowd never comes into it.

No Sabbath in this one, baker. Matthew 13:58 says, "And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief." That's the reason the text gives. No day of the week is mentioned in these verses.
